blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and September 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 61 in June to 50 in September (−18.0%), and it took 14.7% of the city’s 116 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 22 in June to 13 in September (−40.9%), and it took 20.0% of the city’s 35 sales over the period.

The monthly write-ups singled out Annieville for detached houses in June, July, August (a buyers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in June, September (a sellers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in July (a buyers’ best bet).

Established fee-simple stock: an established residential area of predominantly single detached houses, mostly freehold detached and duplex lots. The former North Delta Area Plan identified residential infill east of 116 Street between 90 Avenue and 96 Avenue. Fee-simple is the default form here: the owner owns the lot outright, with no strata, no Form B and no strata fees.

Lot character from the zone ladder, as the City states it: RD3 at a 4,000 m² minimum lot, RS6 at 390 m² (width 13 m, depth 30 m) and RS1 at 4,000 m² (width 30 m, average depth 30 m, maximum one single detached dwelling per lot); the full bylaw ladder runs RS1/RS2/RS3/RD2/RD3 at 4,000 m², RS4 at 610 m², RS5 at 550 m² or 460 m², RS6 at 390 m², RS7 at 335 m², RD1 at 836 m² and RD4 at 504 m², and there is no RD5 zone. These are zone minimums, not a claim that every Annieville lot is that size — confirm the parcel's zone on the City maps.

: a City bylaw notice for 10604 River Road proposed rezoning from Duplex/Single Detached Residential 3 (RD3) to Single Detached Residential 6 (RS6) for a two-lot subdivision under Bylaw No. 7600 — an example of the large-lot-to-small-lot infill pattern on the River Road side. This address is cited as the City's own documented example of how subdivision happens here; it is not presented as a for-sale lot offering.

Bare-land strata: none verified: Where a bare-land strata did exist, it would be strata tenure in full — Form B / strata fees / bylaws apply to the lot — but no such plan is documented for Annieville, so no bare-land strata claim is made.

Named development — built-form project, not a lot offering: Annieville Heights, duplex homes in Annieville by Fika Developments and Satori Homes, is the named current project for the area (developer source). It is documented here by name only as the research states it — duplex homes, not bare lots — and its civic address is UNVERIFIED (developer source only). Do not present it as a lot subdivision.
Cross-reference only — Delta Gardens: Not Annieville land stock; no lot character, count or price is stated for it here.

ALR vs non-ALR: land in the ALR inside Annieville was not confirmed in the sources read — ALR status is a property-specific check through the Agricultural Land Commission, and no ALR percentage split is stated.

Serviced vs unserviced: no well/septic position is documented for Annieville lots in the research; parcel-level servicing for a single lot is UNCONFIRMED here and is confirmed with the City at subdivision. Do not assume a large river-side parcel is serviced for its subdivided form until the City answers.
Land assemblies / rezoning proposals: No other assembly or development site is documented for Annieville in the research.

Market context, labelled correctly: Annieville detached inventory 50 / solds 5 and Condos & Townhomes inventory 13 / solds 2 in September 2026 (SnapStats FVR September 2026 report); North Delta community detached median $1,100,000. SnapStats has NO land category (Detached vs "Condos & Townhomes" combined; North Delta is a SnapStats-covered community, cited here as community context only) — no detached figure is presented as a land figure. Sub-area median prices: UNVERIFIED (SnapStats publishes medians at community level only).

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Annieville

items.t: Annieville is in north-west North Delta, in the City of Delta, along the Fraser River frontage. 3950). The City publishes no street-by-street written boundary; the former plan map shows Annieville along River Road, with 116 Street at its east side and the Fraser River at its north side.
Nearby areas: Nordel to the east and south-east, Tilbury industrial lands to the west along River Road, the Fraser River to the north.
Main roads: River Road runs along the Fraser River frontage; 112 Street and 116 Street run south to Nordel Way and Highway 91 / Alex Fraser Bridge access; Scott Road (120 Street) is to the east.

Transit: route 312 runs Scott Road Station to Scottsdale Exchange via Scott Road, 96 Avenue, 114 Street, 92A Avenue, 112 Street and 72 Avenue; route 391 runs Scott Road Station to Scottsdale Exchange via 72 Avenue, 116 Street and 96 Avenue; both connect to the Expo Line at Scott Road Station.

Schools: School District 37 catchments are address-based. For the sample address 9240 112 Street, Delta, the SD37 School Locator result is Annieville Elementary (K–7), 9240 112 St., and Delview Secondary (8–12), 9111 116 St.; the locator shows no middle-school category, and catchments for other addresses must be checked in the locator. This is a sample-address locator result documented in the research — not a settled chain for the whole sub-area.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Annieville

items.t: Escarpment / hazard rule — first-order for river-side lots: the Fraser River frontage is in the ND1 Fraser River Escarpment Development Permit Area; the OCP states that area is subject to mud flows, debris flows, erosion, land slip and subsidence, and that river bank and ravine slopes are subject to erosion. Geotechnical review belongs in the subject list for a frontage lot.

ALR rules (where an ALR parcel is confirmed — none confirmed in Annieville in the research): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha); BC Assessment farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR. Check the parcel with the ALC first.

Delta property taxes and utilities: City of Delta 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on balances outstanding after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after September 2, 2026; the approved 2026 Financial Plan included a 2.9% property tax increase for City operational services. Delta's 2026 flat-rate utility fee is $1,658 for a single-family home. Area-specific levy notes for Annieville: UNVERIFIED.

River Road is both the view and the working route: River Road is the neighbourhood's frontage street and a working route toward the Tilbury industrial lands — flag truck volumes and noise expectations early on frontage lots.

The commercial pocket has its own permit area: the Annieville commercial village on River Road is covered by the ND3 Annieville Development Permit Area in the 2024 OCP and provides local services; a grocery store named with its street address in an official City source: UNVERIFIED.

The park beside the school is a live City project: Annieville Lions Park, 9150 112 Street, sits beside Annieville Elementary, and the City has an Annieville Lions Park Master Plan project. George Mackie Library (Fraser Valley Regional Library), 8440 112th Street, is just east in Nordel; no recreation centre inside Annieville was confirmed — the North Delta Recreation Centre at 11415 84 Avenue serves North Delta from Nordel.
The nearest hospital is across Delta: Delta Hospital, 5800 Mountain View Blvd, Delta, in Ladner (Fraser Health); the North Delta Public Health Unit is at 11245 84 Avenue, Delta.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Annieville than in June?
faq.a: In Annieville, listings of houses fell from 61 in June to 50 in September (−18.0%); condos and townhomes fell from 22 in June to 13 in September (−40.9%).

faq.q: How big is Annieville compared with the rest of North Delta?
faq.a: In September 2026, Annieville held 23.9% of the 209 houses listed in North Delta and 18.3% of the 71 condos and townhomes listed in North Delta.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Annieville from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 17 houses and 7 condos and townhomes sold in Annieville over those 4 months.

faq.q: How do I find out which school serves an address in Annieville?
faq.a: School catchments are set by address, so use the school district's catchment locator with the exact address. Catchment lines change, so check before you write an offer.

faq.q: Who can help me buy or sell in Annieville?
faq.a: Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, works across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361 or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: What land actually trades in Annieville?
faq.a: Fee-simple house lots — established detached/duplex lots, and large river-side parcels whose value turns on splitting them. No bare-land strata and no named bare-land subdivision was verified.

faq.q: How big are the big river-side lots, really?
faq.a: The zones that carry them — RD3 and RS1 — both set a 4,000 m² minimum lot; RS6, the small-lot zone they split into, sets 390 m² (width 13 m, depth 30 m). Confirm the individual parcel's zone on the City maps.

faq.q: How does a big lot become two lots here?
faq.a: By rezoning plus subdivision — the City's own documented example is 10604 River Road, proposed from RD3 to RS6 for a two-lot subdivision under Bylaw No. 7600. Price the rezoning and servicing answer, not just the house.

faq.q: Can I add a suite or coach house instead of subdividing?
faq.a: Delta's SSMUH rules allow combinations of single detached dwellings, duplex dwellings, secondary suites, coach houses and garden suites where the bylaw applies (Bylaws 8394+8395, adopted June 24, 2024) — confirm the parcel's zone sheet before promising a configuration.

faq.q: Is the river frontage a hazard area?
faq.a: Yes — the ND1 Fraser River Escarpment Development Permit Area covers the frontage, and the OCP lists mud flows, debris flows, erosion, land slip and subsidence for that area. Geotechnical review belongs in the subjects.
